title: Local tensor roof for two augmented resolutions
statement: Let i:Z\to Y be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with additive tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Fix opens V in Z and U in Y, and arbitrary cochain complexes P,K,S on Y [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Write F for termwise open restriction to U, and G for tensor pullback along i followed by restriction to V and its over site W=V intersect i^{-1}(U) [lem-sc-homology-evaluation-formal-complex]. Suppose a:F(P)\to F(S) and b:F(K)\to F(S) are both K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Then there are a complex L on W's over site and quasi-isomorphisms q:L\to G(P), p:L\to G(K) [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. No freeness, zero differential, bound, Koszul sequence, affine chart, or closed immersion hypothesis is assumed. The vertex L may depend on both augmentations.

source.place: Proof of independence of K-flat representatives; Tag 06YI derived pullback and composition with open restriction.

proof.text: The two augmentations identify F(P) and F(K) in D(U). Apply Mathlib DerivedCategory.right_fac to this isomorphism, obtaining actual chain maps from a common vertex. The first is a quasi-isomorphism by construction; the second is one by DerivedCategory.isIso_Q_map_iff_quasiIso, since its image is a composite of isomorphisms. Replace the vertex by a K-flat resolution and compose with both maps.

Apply inverse image along the restriction of i over U. It is exact and preserves K-flatness, as the ringed-space pullback theorem applied with the inverse-image ring sheaf shows. Extension of scalars to the source structure sheaf preserves each quasi-isomorphism between these K-flat complexes. This gives the tensor-pulled roof on i^{-1}(U).

Restrict the roof to V intersect i^{-1}(U) and to the over site. Exact restriction preserves its quasi-isomorphisms. The inverse-image and extension-of-scalars formulas identify its endpoints with G(P) and G(K), because all opens in question map into U. Compose with those endpoint isomorphisms. Empty opens give zero complexes. K=0 can satisfy b only if F(S) is acyclic.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_local_kflat_tensor_roof
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [(Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).Additive]
    (V : Z.Opens) (U : Y.Opens) (P K S : CochainComplex Y.Modules ℤ) :
    let F := (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    let G := (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
      moduleOpenOverComplexFunctor Z V (V.ι ⁻¹ᵁ (i ⁻¹ᵁ U))
    ∀ (a : F.obj P ⟶ F.obj S) (b : F.obj K ⟶ F.obj S),
      CochainComplex.IsKFlatResolution (R := U.toScheme.sheaf) a →
      CochainComplex.IsKFlatResolution (R := U.toScheme.sheaf) b →
      ∃ (L : CochainComplex
          (SheafOfModules (V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf.over (V.ι ⁻¹ᵁ (i ⁻¹ᵁ U)))) ℤ)
        (q : L ⟶ G.obj P) (p : L ⟶ G.obj K), QuasiIso q ∧ QuasiIso p
